title: LINQ — concept map
intro: Language Integrated Query (LINQ) lets you filter, transform, and combine collections with either SQL-like keywords or method chains. Both spellings compile to the same operators. Understanding deferred execution, IEnumerable versus IQueryable, and LINQ to Objects versus remote providers is essential for writing correct, performant queries.

overviewDiagram.title: LINQ query lifecycle
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[Data source\nList, array, IQueryable] --> B[Build query\nquery or method syntax]
  B --> C[Deferred plan\nno work yet]
  C --> D{Execute?}
  D -->|foreach / ToList / Count| E[Run operators]
  E --> F{Source type}
  F -->|IEnumerable| G[LINQ to Objects\nFunc delegates in process]
  F -->|IQueryable| H[Provider translates\nexpression tree]

conceptCards.title: Query vs method syntax
conceptCards.summary: from/where/select compiles to Where/Select. No performance difference. Some operators (Count, ToList) are method-only.
conceptCards.example: from x in items where x.Active select x.Name ≡ items.Where(x => x.Active).Select(x => x.Name)

conceptCards.title: Standard operators
conceptCards.summary: SelectMany flattens. GroupBy buffers. Join is inner equijoin with equals. GroupJoin + DefaultIfEmpty is left outer.

conceptCards.title: Deferred execution
conceptCards.summary: A query variable stores a plan. Each enumeration re-runs it. ToList snapshots once. Count then foreach is two passes.
conceptCards.example: var q = items.Where(x => x.Active); // no work until foreach or ToList

conceptCards.title: IEnumerable vs IQueryable
conceptCards.summary: IEnumerable uses Func delegates (in-process). IQueryable uses expression trees (provider may translate). AsQueryable on a List is still in-memory.

conceptCards.title: LINQ to Objects
conceptCards.summary: Full C# in lambdas on in-memory data. Remote providers accept a subset. Materialize with ToList before using rich C#.
